thread.title: Axon Enterprise: Values Speak Louder Than Numbers - Axon Enterprise, Inc. (NASDAQ:AAXN)

author: Jenks Jumps
title: Axon Enterprise: Values Speak Louder Than Numbers - Axon Enterprise, Inc. (NASDAQ:AAXN)
text:
There are some companies that are simply enjoyable to follow. Typically, I'm drawn to industry disruptors, especially when the company is embracing technology to do the disrupting. Axon Enterprises ( AAXN ) is focused on being a disruptor in the law enforcement and public safety arenas.
When Axon Enterprise was doing business as Taser International, its primary products were tasers or conducted electrical weapons [CEW] and reloadable cartridges. Body cameras and in-car cameras were the next hardware offerings and prompted the company's name change. The need to access, transfer, track, organize, retrieve, share and manage digital evidence captured by cameras drove Axon's development of a cloud-based application, Evidence.com . So, sales of software and services followed with an emphasis on generating recurring revenue. Applying artificial intelligence and analytics to the vast store of digital evidence is underway.
In November 2017, Axon projected its compound annual growth rate for revenue would range from 16% to 20% for the next three to five years and would range from 15% to 18% for the next five to seven years. The growth was to come through both the continuing development of hardware, software and solutions as well as geographic expansion. Source
Credibility In 2018, Axon Enterprise established pages and pages of credibility, at least in my book.
The first evidence is visible in the company's performance. On February 27, 2018, founder and CEO, Patrick “Rick” Smith, accepted his last paycheck and switched to a performance compensation package based on stock options when the company reported 2017 full-year results. For Mr. Smith to be compensated fully , Axon must achieve a market cap milestone as well as any 12 of 16 identified financial milestones. The market cap milestone includes 12 tranches growing from $2.5 billion to $13.5 billion. The second set of milestones is based on operational metrics and divided into two targets – revenue growth and EBITDA growth. Revenue targets grow from $700 million to $2 billion. Adjusted EBITDA targets grow from $125 million to $230 million. Source
Annual revenue in 2017 was $343.8 million and adjusted EBITDA was $40.72 million. These numbers, basically, represent the starting points for Mr. Smith's compensation plan. Through the third quarter of 2018, year-to-date revenue totals $305.3 million and year-to-date adjusted EBITDA totals $50.5 million.
“As we approach the final months of the year, we're tracking to hit the midpoint of our revenue guidance.”
The second set of evidence validates Axon's core values. Source
Be Obsessed With its roots embedded with law enforcement, Axon Enterprise's “walk with the customer” has been telling. Mr. Smith views his company as an “agent of reform”.
“We can complain about what police are doing, or we can step in and address it and help solve the problems.”
For example, the adoption of body cameras found citizen complaints dropping significantly, guilty pleas increasing and officers spending far less time in court. As well, use of force incidents by officers also decreased. In other words, both sides, citizen and protector/enforcer, reap the benefit.
In early October, the International Association of Chiefs of Police (IACP) held its annual conference in Orlando. Axon Enterprise is a corporate partner. The company sponsored a tribute video accompanied by a live performance from One Republic (sponsored by Verizon ( VZ )). The video clearly communicates to the company's customers that Axon gets it.
Mr. Smith's obsession, to make the world a safer place and transform how public safety professionals perform their jobs, anchors the company's second core value.
Aim Far For years, Rick Smith has challenged his R&D team to “make the bullet obsolete”. His target device is a non-lethal weapon that won't just replace a gun but will “outperform a pistol”. With body cameras and fleet cameras intended to help de-escalate situations, he portends the need for deadly weapons naturally declines.
“We are the tech company that’s going to make the world less violent.”
A stronger presence on the streets should also help. With a cloud-based platform for storing digital evidence and AI for processing it, law enforcement professionals will spend less time at their keyboards filing forms. As far back as the 2015 IACP conference in Chicago, Axon was championing “a future with no paperwork in which bullets were obsolete”.
Its most recent iteration of a CEW is dramatically closer to its vision. At the 2018 IACP conference, it introduced the seventh generation of the Taser product line, TASER 7. The weapon is improved, more effective and is fully integrated with Axon's software. Much of the 2018 third quarter earnings call was spent discussing the company's new products because of their customers' reception of the dramatic potential impact.
“We essentially reinvented the TASER weapon from the ground up. We looked at all the factors that can lead to an ineffective use and engineered significant improvements on each of those factors.
We rigorously analyze the reasons why bullets can be more effective and more reliable than a TASER weapon. And we looked at all the technical limitations and then invented ways to overcome those limitations to make the TASER weapon more effective.”
The weapon is available now. Despite a ground-up redesign, Axon does still believe the product line is a decade away from making the bullet obsolete. But, that doesn't make the product any less transformative.
“Law enforcement customers across the board tell us that TASER 7 is a game changer.”
The company also introduced the Axon Body 3 at the conference. The new body camera offers better capture features and provides real-time situational awareness through live-streaming and GPS functionality. Evidence is uploaded through built-in LTE networking capabilities. The product also integrates AI-capabilities such as gunshot detection.
“When you take a camera and turn it into a live connected sensor, all of a sudden, it's not just something that can help you after the event, it can help you during the event and with real-time information.”
The Axon Body 3 is expected to start shipping in the summer of 2019.
In addition to the new hardware generations, Axon Enterprise introduced a records management offering to help customers benefit from the products' connectivity and integration.
Join Forces The forces of interconnectivity and capturing evidence are setting Axon apart from competitors as well as changing its customers' workflow. TASER 7 will enable Axon's concept of offering the CEW product line as part of a service because of its integration with the company's software platform. For customers purchasing TASER 7 and Axon Body 3 on an Officer Safety Plan before the end of 2019, Axon will provide five years of free access to its records management system.
It is also pertinent to understand Axon's strategy regarding connectivity. Axon's new devices are integrated to use FirstNet, an LTE network recently built by Verizon and AT&T ( T ) dedicated to first responders nationwide. With an ongoing adoption of the use of FirstNet by first responders, Axon is positioning itself as the go-to provider for devices that will “work” on the network and gaining first-mover advantages.
Integration, connectivity and affordable access are not the only indicators of Axon's partnering mentality.
Own It In the past two months, Axon's core value of commiting, taking action and delivering has been on the line with the largest police department in the United States
After somewhat contentious interactions as competitors, in May 2018, Axon Enterprise announced the acquisition of VIEVU.
Just a few years ago, as Taser International, Axon competed with VIEVU for the NYPD contract for body cameras. VIEVU won the contract based on price. With the acquisition, Axon assumed responsibility for the NYPD as a customer.
In October, a VIEVU LE-5 worn by a New York City officer ignited . The New York City Police Department, in reaction, pulled 2,990 body cameras off the chests of police officers. Axon immediately offered its assistance with the investigation.
In the third quarter earnings call , Axon provided an update on the findings and the resolution.
“Our analysis says it's not a defective product.
The incident report that came back showed that this was a battery that was damaged, basically, with a paper clip being inserted aggressively and puncturing through the wall and the battery cell. We are also making some modifications to make that more bulletproof.”
That customer will accelerate their transition from VIEVU cameras to Axon Body 2 cameras and Axon Evidence.”
Beyond assistance with the investigation and resolution, Axon will also be taking a hit financially.
“We may have some cost absorption associated with this move in Q4. We're actively working to minimize the impact to our Q4 P&L. But, we believe we can absorb a material amount of expense and still produce adjusted EBITDA margins for the full year within our guidance of 14% to 16%.”
The decision was made in line with Axon's core value of “owning it”.
“Right now, this is all about helping an important customer that had a challenging situation. And we're investing in the relationship. So this does not create any short-term revenue opportunities. But we believe one of the things that makes us different is we do not allow programs to fail. And I think that's what we're demonstrating with the customer in question here.”
Expect Candor By scouring its customers' work environments in search of areas to retool, rework and redefine, Axon reaps valuable information that tools or technology cannot address. As a result, Axon developed Axon Academy to develop effective training methods. At the 2018 IACP conference, in addition to its hardware and software introductions, the company also introduced its latest training program. It, of course, addresses the new hardware. But, the redesigned offering also incorporates de-escalation methods as well as empathy training for special needs populations.
“A 2018 study conducted by Wakefield Research found that more than four in five law enforcement personnel say they want better training to de-escalate situations. Nine in ten respondents agree that improved training on less-lethal tools, such as CEWs, would result in reduced uses-of-force in the field.”
True to its nature, Axon is embracing technology even in its training offering. It is offered online as well as through mobile devices. And, this latest version employs virtual reality.
Wrapping Up 2018 In the third quarter , Axon's total revenue set a record at $104.8 million. Just as importantly, annual recurring revenue broke through the $100 million mark. At $101.6 million, it has improved 60% year-over-year.
The transition to TASER 7 is expected to ramp in 2019. This may potentially slow hardware revenue in the 2018 fourth quarter even though the quarter has typically been a stronger one for hardware sales. Regardless, Axon is expecting full-year revenue in excess of $405 million, reflecting an 18% gain over 2017. Adjusted EBITDA at a margin of 15% would then equal approximately $61 million.
And, yet, this impressive performance in 2018 is but the beginning. As well, the totals are still substantially lower than the first steps of the compensation package - $700 million in revenue or $125 million in adjusted EBITDA.
Investment Considerations The change to Mr. Smith's compensation package attracted the market's attention earlier in the year . The share price exploded from the $28 range and what could be considered an irrational momentum carried it to a high over $76 in the summer. It's not entirely clear why some would expect a multi-year plan to transpire in just months. Whether it was due to common sense or market turmoil, the share price is now trading approximately 40% lower.
Cloud Strategies purports SaaS revenue (software as a service) or annual recurring revenue should be valued greater than product revenue. The weighted average for the P/S (price-to-sales) ratio for publicly-traded SaaS companies is 8.7. There's probably no other company more hotly debated than Apple ( AAPL ) as to whether it should be valued as a services company or product company. Its price-to-sales ratio pales by comparison at approximately 3.25.
Recognizing the potential revenue contributions from new hardware such as the TASER 7 and Axon Body 3 as well as other Axon developments, the growth projection for 2019 becomes easily believable. With credibility in mind, the 2017 projection for 16% to 20% in revenue growth for three to five years makes Axon investable.
Using a sum-of-the-parts valuation based on a 2019 revenue estimate of $485 million, Axon's share price does appear fairly valued in the mid-$40 range.

But, one could easily argue investing in Axon Enterprise isn't solely about purchasing shares of a growth stock at a fair value. Many investors would relish finding a trustworthy company to believe in for several years forward. If there's a takeaway from observing Axon Enterprise, especially in this last quarter of 2018, it would be that the company is certainly true to its values. Its core values do speak louder than numbers.
 AAXN.
Additional disclosure: I belong to an investment club that owns shares in AAXN.
